Article Title: ‘India is not Bangladesh or France’: Tharoor hits back at BJP, says opposition backs peaceful protest
Article Text:
‘We believe in peaceful protest’: Tharoor rejects BJP’s India-Bangladesh comparison

Political row over ‘regime change’

Tharoor comments on Musk's Starlink remarks

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Monday rejected comparisons between India and Bangladesh or France amid the political row over the opposition's use of the phrase “regime change”, asserting that the demand was for free and fair elections and not an attempt to topple the government.Responding to Union minister Kiren Rijiju's remarks, Tharoor said India did not support violence and that protests should remain peaceful. He also questioned the relevance of comparisons with unrest in other countries."I think that India is not Bangladesh and India is not France. I don't see these analogies as particularly relevant... We would never condone any of the violence, setting alight buses and police stations and so on, that has occurred in France. We only believe in peaceful protest... that's the kind of protest that I have participated in, and that I believe the opposition in general supports... As far as the larger issues are concerned, there's no point distorting a phrase like 'regime change' and so on. .. What we are calling for is free and fair elections... What is troubling today is that large numbers of people have been cut from the electoral rolls as the result of a completely troublesome, irregular, and partially illegal process.This is why we are calling for all this to be undone... It's a constitutional issue. It's not an issue of trying to topple a regime or anything like that..."Tharoor also defended citizens' right to protect democratic institutions, while clarifying that his criticism was directed at their functioning and not their existence."...Democracy is not a gift of anybody... we, the ordinary citizens of India, are the custodians of it... Every Indian citizen has the right to protect our democracy... All I'm saying is we are asking institutions like the Election Commission to behave themselves, to perform as they are required to by the democratic Constitution of India. That's all it is. I'm not in any way challenging these institutions as institutions. I'm challenging the way they are behaving, the way they are conducting themselves, and that is something that honestly all of us in India should be concerned about..."The remarks came amid a political exchange over protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.On Sunday, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju alleged that “anti-India groups” and some politicians had colluded to provoke young people and spread violence, claiming that a conspiracy similar to the unrest in Bangladesh and France had been planned in India.“The violent incident that occurred in Bangladesh and the riots, arson, and looting that took place in France, a similar conspiracy was hatched for India as well,” Rijiju said in a post on X.He further asserted that a change of government in India could take place only through elections.“Regime change in India is absolutely possible, but only through elections, not through Soros,” he said.The row intensified after senior advocate Prashant Bhushan described the agitation against Kumar as a “fight for regime change”. All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora also referred to the Gen Z-led movement in Bangladesh.Rijiju had earlier accused political rivals and activists of using street protests to create unrest and destabilise constitutional institutions. He said India's youth were focused on nation-building rather than political upheaval.Separately, Tharoor responded to Elon Musk's recent remarks regarding Starlink, saying the government had maintained that all companies bidding for the service were going through the same process and facing similar delays."I've heard the government's explanation on this issue, which is that there is a process and that all the companies bidding for this are in the same process and are facing the same delays. If that position of the government is taken literally, that means Musk is no further behind in the queue, and Ambani is no further ahead. I think we just have to wait for the process to play itself out... There are several factors. There are questions of the technology, certain security concerns, various kinds of details to do with the uplinking and finally cost.The last one, the ordinary public will decide. If you are giving me a service and he's giving it to me for 10 times the price, I may take it from you. Or if I really feel that what he's doing is worth 10 times the money, I'll give it to him. Each subscriber will have to decide. Personally, I'm quite happy with my regular connections. I'm not looking for a Starlink myself. But if there are people who feel these things are useful, in a free country, let them have the opportunity."
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor rejects comparisons between India and Bangladesh or France. He says India does not support violence and that protests should remain peaceful. The remarks came amid a political exchange over protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and allegations of irregularities.

Article Title: 6 in 10 men over 45 unaware of their prostate cancer screening status: Survey
Article Text:
​69% unable to name a single risk factor; only 1 in 6 report ever being screened​

NEW DELHI:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nearly six in 10 Indian men aged 45 and above do not know whether they have ever been screened for prostate cancer, while only around one in six report having undergone screening, a survey by NGO Heal Foundation has found.The survey of 1,036 men across Delhi-NCR, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana and Maharashtra points to significant gaps in awareness of prostate cancer risk factors, screening and when to seek medical advice. Nearly 69% of respondents could not name a single risk factor, while only 13.2% recognised family history as one. Around three-fourths believed prostate cancer monitoring should begin only at age 50 or later.The findings highlight a disconnect between routine healthcare and prostate-specific awareness. Although 62% of respondents said they underwent annual health check-ups, 60.8% did not know their prostate cancer screening status and only about 16% reported having ever been screened.Awareness of the prostate-specific antigen (PSA) blood test was also limited. Only around 31% had heard of PSA as a marker, and just 14% had specifically requested the test.“These findings point to a fundamental awareness gap around prostate cancer,” said Dr Devavrat Arya, vice-chairman, medical oncology, Max Healthcare, Delhi. He said awareness of risk factors, screening and when to consult a doctor needed to become a more visible part of routine health conversations among men over 45.The survey found that 59.5% of men were uncomfortable discussing screening or treatment with doctors, while only 18% would initiate the conversation themselves. Although 67% trusted doctors and hospitals, just 36% identified a urologist as the appropriate specialist. Meanwhile, 84% searched online or on social media for health information.The biggest barriers to screening were believing it was unnecessary (34%), having no symptoms (28%) and not receiving a doctor's recommendation (22%). Cost (19%), embarrassment or privacy concerns (17%), fear of diagnosis (14%) and not knowing where to go (11%) were other reasons.Gaps widened with age: around 72% of men aged 65 and above were unsure of their screening status, while 80% reported low treatment knowledge. Overall, 71.2% had limited knowledge of treatment options, only 10% felt confident across the treatment pathway, and 44% wanted a second opinion before treatment.Dr Nitesh Rohatgi, principal director of medical oncology at fortis memorial research institute, said symptoms in older men were often dismissed as ageing, delaying diagnosis, while awareness of advanced treatments such as radioligand therapy remained limited even after diagnosis.The findings highlight the need for greater risk awareness and informed discussions with doctors. However, the survey reflects self-reported awareness and screening experiences, not prostate cancer prevalence or screening rates among all Indian men.
Article Summary: Survey of 1,036 men across Delhi-NCR, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana and Maharashtra points to significant gaps in awareness of prostate cancer risk factors, screening and when to seek medical advice. Nearly 69% of respondents could not name a single risk factor, while only 13.2% recognised family history as one.

Article Title: Shots fired at Tiger Shroff, actor's driver hurt; Bishnoi gang claims responsibility - top developments
Article Text:
Lawrence Bishnoi gang claims responsibility

Police launch massive manhunt

Fadnavis directs Mumbai Police to expedite probe

Rohit Shetty, Salman Khan among film personalities targeted

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Unknown gunmen opened fire at actor Tiger Shroff on Sunday, injuring his driver and another person, an autorickshaw driver. The incident took place near Mumbai's Pushpa Park, within the limits of Juhu police station in the western suburb.According to police, the actor escaped unhurt, while his driver, identified as Firdaus, sustained an injury to his left hand."The chain of events leading to the incident is being pieced together," a police official said."Shroff is safe and has not sustained any injuries in the firing incident. His driver, identified as Firdaus, and another driver of the autorickshaw, identified only as Chauhan, were injured in the shooting and were rushed for medical treatment," the official added.Shroff and his driver were taken to Nanavati Hospital in Vile Parle. Doctors said the actor had sustained a few abrasions but no bullet wounds.The third person was taken to Cooper Hospital after sustaining bullet injuries to his chest.Meanwhile, Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, purportedly associated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, claimed responsibility for the attack."Ram Ram to all the brothers. Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu take responsibility for what happened to Tiger Shroff today.We had called him and tried to explain things to him, but he did not understand. So today, we made him understand properly," Anil Pandit said in a Facebook post."Anyone in the Mumbai film industry who does not listen to us or works with Salman Khan will be next. Wait and watch."Note: And those dogs from other groups who think they can gain fame by using our name - we will soon kill them and make them famous."Salute to the martyrs," he added.The authenticity of the claims and their alleged link to the firing had yet to be independently established. Police are investigating the incident and examining the available evidence to determine the motive behind the shooting.Meanwhile, Mumbai Police has launched a manhunt to nab those involved in the incident. Specialised teams are examining CCTV footage from the area for leads."The incident occurred while Tiger Shroff was returning in his car. He was not hit by any bullets and is completely safe. Mumbai Police has formed multiple teams and initiated further action. The forensic team has begun its preliminary analysis, with approximately 15 teams currently working on the case," DCP Mohit Garg said."Further information will be shared as it becomes available. As I mentioned, the forensic team is carrying out its investigation. At this stage, it would not be appropriate to disclose specific details regarding the number of rounds fired," he added.Meanwhile, Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis called the Mumbai Police commissioner to seek details about the firing incident.He directed the commissioner to expedite the investigation and take strict action against those responsible.Fadnavis also called Tiger Shroff and spoke with him.He assured him, saying, “We are all with you. We will trace and apprehend the accused at the earliest.”Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde also condemned the incident and said Mumbai Police has formed several teams to track down those who opened fire. He added that the accused will be given a response in their own language."Tiger Shroff’s vehicle was targeted. This incident is deeply concerning and condemnable; I condemn it in the strongest possible terms. I have spoken with the Police Commissioner, and I have also spoken with Tiger Shroff. The Mumbai Police Commissioner has formed several teams to track down those who opened fire—they will be apprehended and given a response in their own language. Our current priority is to keep Mumbai and its citizens safe. Whether it is a celebrity or an ordinary citizen, ensuring their safety is the responsibility of the police and the government, and there will be no negligence in this regard," Shinde said."No gang will be spared; we will not let them get away with this. We have seen large-scale gang wars like this before, back in the 1990s. Even then, the Mumbai Police effectively handled the situation—they dealt with the perpetrators in their own language, ensuring that law and order were maintained. So, any gang attempting to spread terror here should think twice. This is Mumbai; this is Maharashtra," he added.Several personalities from the film industry have been targeted in shooting incidents in recent years.In February this year, five rounds were fired outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty's residence in Juhu. The Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the firing.In April 2024, two men on a motorcycle fired five rounds outside actor Salman Khan's Galaxy Apartments in Mumbai's Bandra area.Mumbai Police arrested several suspects linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. The trial against five accused - Vicky Gupta, Sagar Pal, Harpal Singh, Sonukumar Bishnoi and Mohammad Rafiq Choudhari - is underway. The sixth accused, Anuj Kumar Thapan, died in police custody in May 2024.
Article Summary: Unknown gunmen opened fire at actor Tiger Shroff on Sunday, injuring his driver and another person, an autorickshaw driver. The incident took place near Mumbai's Pushpa Park, within the limits of Juhu police station in the western suburb. Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, purportedly associated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, claimed responsibility.

Article Title: The Dimple factor: Can she crack BJP's women-voter fortress?
Article Text:
From Akhilesh’s shadow to SP’s second-in-command

Why Akhilesh needs Dimple

How an SP win could reshape Dimple’s role

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Like many women who marry into political families, Dimple Yadav ’s entry into politics was more a matter of circumstance than choice. She made her electoral debut in 2009 after her husband, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav , vacated the Firozabad Lok Sabha seat, choosing to retain Kannauj after contesting from both constituencies.Despite a star-studded campaign, Dimple lost to Congress candidate Raj Babbar. Since then, however, she has contested five Lok Sabha elections, winning four.Yet, her electoral record did little to dispel the perception that she was a relatively passive player in politics. Within the Samajwadi Party, she was seen as a low-profile figure who complemented her husband from the background. In Parliament, she was often spotted sitting behind Akhilesh, thumping her desk in support of his speeches.For years, Dimple appeared unable (or perhaps unwilling) to step out of her husband’s political shadow.That may now be changing.With the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections approaching, Dimple, who has largely accompanied Akhilesh at party meetings and public gatherings, has been entrusted with an independent political responsibility. The move signals a possible shift in her role as Akhilesh prepares for another bid to return to power at 5, Kalidas Marg, after a decade out of office.Ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, Dimple Yadav is stepping into a more prominent role in the Samajwadi Party. Since Mulayam Singh Yadav’s death in 2022 and the decline of Shivpal Yadav’s influence within the party, she has increasingly emerged as one of its most visible campaigners and a key figure in its leadership.During the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Dimple addressed rallies across more than a dozen constituencies. She also retained Mainpuri, the family stronghold, by a margin of nearly two lakh votes. Her media appearances and social media presence have grown considerably, reflecting a more assertive public role than in the past.Her growing political visibility has extended beyond election campaigns. During the protests over the NEET paper leak in June and July, she emerged at the forefront of the party’s outreach to student protesters. She also led delegations to meet climate activist Sonam Wangchuk during his hunger strike, expressing support for his demands.On July 20, she joined the student-led “Sansad Chalo” protest in New Delhi and was seen tending to injured students after clashes with Delhi Police.While Akhilesh was inside Parliament, Dimple was out on the streets.She has also become a more vocal representative of the party’s position on issues ranging from women’s safety to the alleged embezzlement of donations made to Ayodhya’s Ram temple. Both inside and outside the Lok Sabha, she has sharpened her attacks on the BJP, challenging its claims on governance and social justice.Dimple has also accused the BJP of deliberately delaying the implementation of women’s reservation, despite Parliament passing the legislation in 2023.“When the Bill was tabled in 2023, all political parties supported it and it was passed, which explains that the opposition was in no way against the Bill. If the BJP’s sole intention was reservation to women, they would have implemented the Bill passed in 2023,” she said.“They have other motives behind moving the amendment Bill,” the Mainpuri MP added.Her latest initiative is the proposed Stri Samman Samriddhi Yojana, a scheme aimed at the economic and social empowerment of women that the Samajwadi Party says it will introduce if voted to power in 2027. The proposal promises eligible women an annual payment of Rs 40,000.“Women’s power will develop not merely by talking about it, but by giving women true representation. Respect and prosperity of every woman included in the PDA as ‘Aadhi Abadi’ (women) is our resolve,” Dimple said.“She deserves respect simply because she is a woman. Social empowerment and strengthening her position require respect even before prosperity,” she added.The announcement also places the Samajwadi Party in direct competition with the BJP over women-focused welfare. It came amid reports that the Yogi Adityanath government was considering a direct cash-transfer scheme offering women Rs 50,000.The PDA formula — Pichada, Dalit, Alpasankhyak (backward classes, Dalits and minorities) — helped the Samajwadi Party stage a remarkable comeback in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.After winning just five of Uttar Pradesh’s 80 seats in 2019, the party secured 37 in 2024, emerging as the state’s largest party in the Lok Sabha. It expanded beyond its traditional Muslim-Yadav support base by fielding candidates from non-Yadav OBC and Dalit communities.But replicating that success in an assembly election will require more than maintaining caste arithmetic. As Akhilesh prepares for the high-stakes polls scheduled for early 2027, he is looking to preserve the party’s momentum and widen its appeal further. Women, who cut across caste and religious boundaries, are central to that effort.The scale of the opportunity is considerable. Women account for 45.46% of Uttar Pradesh’s electorate, with 6,09,09,525 registered voters, according to the figures cited by the state’s electoral authorities.They have also consistently turned out in greater numbers than men in recent elections. In the 2022 Assembly polls, women’s turnout stood at around 62.2%, compared with 59.6% among men. The pattern continued in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, when turnout among women was 57.22%, against 56.46% among men.Yet women voters have historically been a weak spot for the Samajwadi Party.According to the Lokniti-CSDS post-poll survey for the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the BJP enjoyed a 13-percentage-point lead over the SP-Rashtriya Lok Dal alliance among women voters.The BJP has also repeatedly invoked the law-and-order record of previous SP governments to portray the party as insensitive to women’s safety. Recalling the period before 2017, chief minister Yogi Adityanath said during a public address in Gorakhpur: “A saying had become popular: ‘Dekh Sapayi, bitiya ghabrayi’.”He alleged that criminals and strongmen under the then government had created an atmosphere of fear, leaving families worried about their daughters’ safety.This is where Dimple could prove politically valuable.Her growing prominence gives the Samajwadi Party a recognisable woman leader who can take its PDA pitch beyond caste coalitions and make aadhi abadi — women, or half the population — a more visible part of its political strategy. She can serve as the face of its outreach to women, amplify its welfare promises and challenge the BJP’s claim to be the more women-friendly party.She also offers the SP a way to counter its longstanding image problem on law and order. Unlike the party’s male leadership, which continues to face the BJP’s allegations of mafia-gunda raj, Dimple has no comparable political baggage. Her public persona is less confrontational, potentially allowing the party to project a more measured and inclusive image without abandoning its attacks on the ruling party.Her role could also help the SP challenge the BJP on women’s representation and welfare on more equal political terms.Rather than relying solely on Akhilesh to make the case, the party now has a prominent woman leader with electoral credibility, national visibility and a place within its inner circle.Dimple’s Rajput background could offer another avenue for outreach beyond the party’s traditional support base. Whether that translates into wider support among Rajputs, however, remains uncertain.A return to power in Uttar Pradesh could further transform Dimple’s position, both within the Samajwadi Party and in national politics.If Akhilesh becomes chief minister, Dimple could assume a more substantial role in Parliament and potentially take on greater responsibility for coordinating the party’s parliamentary strategy. A stronger organisational position could also put her at the centre of the SP’s outreach to women and communities beyond its traditional support base.Such a shift would mark a significant departure from the role she occupied for much of her political career: a low-profile MP whose public identity was closely tied to her husband’s.But greater visibility does not automatically translate into electoral gains. Dimple’s prominence could help the SP soften its image, challenge the BJP’s women-centric welfare politics and give its promises on representation and economic empowerment a more credible public face. Whether she can materially alter voting patterns, however, remains an open question.Uttar Pradesh is expected to vote in February-March 2027 to elect a 403-member assembly, though the Election Commission has yet to announce the official schedule.In the 2022 assembly elections, the BJP won 255 seats, securing a second consecutive term in power. The BJP-led NDA won 273 seats, while the Samajwadi Party secured 111, a significant improvement on its tally of 47 in 2017. The Congress was reduced to just two seats, down from seven in the previous election.For Akhilesh, the next election will be a test of whether the coalition he built in 2024 can be sustained and expanded. For Dimple, it could be an opportunity to establish herself as more than a trusted political companion and emerge as an independent force in the party’s bid for power.
Article Summary: Dimple Yadav made her electoral debut in 2009 after her husband, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, vacated the Firozabad Lok Sabha seat. Since then, she has contested five Lok Sabha elections, winning four. Her media appearances and social media presence have grown considerably.

Article Title: Is college worth it in 2026
Article Text:
Representaitve AI image

In our twenties, when there is still so much time ahead of us, time that seems ample for a hundred indecisions, for a hundred visions and revisions—we draw a card, and we must decide right then and there whether to keep that card and discard the next, or discard the first card and keep the second. And before we know it, the deck has been played out and the decisions we have just made will shape our lives for decades to come. Rules of Civility, Amor Towles

On self-learning

Why do we go to university?

A Bend in the River

opportunity of discovering yourself

Schooling may not only affect income but also the degree to which one enjoys working or the likelihood of not being able to find work. Schooling could also lead individuals to make better decisions about health, marriage, and parenting style. It may have significant consumption value too. And, as we argue in this paper, schooling may affect preferences in a way that makes individuals more patient, more goal-oriented, and less likely to engage in risky behavior. In short, schooling may have important nonpecuniary returns. — Philip Oreopoulos and Kjell G. Salvanes, “Priceless: The Nonpecuniary Benefits of Schooling”

Again, you can’t connect the dots looking forward. You can only connect them looking backwards, so you have to trust that the dots will somehow connect in your future.

The pay gap between having a university degree and not having one

-

Many years ago, I went to my parents expressing my wish to drop a year to prepare for IIT-JEE. It was a particularly stressful time for us financially, and yet, my parents did not think twice before fully supporting me in this risky endeavour. As grateful as I am to my parents, I am probably not unique. As I entered IIT Kharagpur the following year, I met several others who came through very humble backgrounds, students whose parents had pledged their land, or taken an extra job or a loan to provide the best opportunities to their children. For most parents, the choice was self-evident. A good undergraduate degree was a way to move up the social ladder.But lately, people have started questioning the worth of a university education. They contend that the university model is outdated today due to rapid technological advancements. In particular, given that we can now learn everything online using AI, we do not need a university degree. And in any case, the pay gap between those with a degree and those without no longer justifies the ever-rising costs.This view is wrong on three counts. First, it overstates the challenge that awaits us because it ignores the harsh reality of people’s ability to learn on their own.Second, it misses what learning at a university entails. And finally, the pay gap it disputes is still very much there.First, questions like whether our existing methods of teaching, working, and thinking are suited to the looming changes are hardly new. When computers arrived, apocalyptic prophecies about employment prospects were ubiquitous. Those arguing that the knowledge from a university degree is redundant over a person’s career miss the point that this is how it has always been. A person graduating in 1980 would have barely seen a computer. In 2005, they might not have known how to work without one. A person graduating in 1990 in India would most likely not have known what an email was; in 2020, their entire workflow would have been online. It is tempting to think this time is different. But, as they say, the more things change, the more they stay the same. A good university education teaches us how to learn and not what to learn. Neither AI nor most jobs will teach that.And what is the historical track record of self-learning? Top scholars from the world’s best universities like Stanford and MIT have made knowledge freely available for nearly two decades now. Gilbert Strang, one of the giants of linear algebra (the field that is at the heart of machine learning and AI), has a course on Linear Algebra on YouTube . The first lecture has 4.9 million views. By the last lecture, we have about 200K-250K views. A macroeconomics course drops from 860K to 15K, a deep learning course drops from 518K to 4.7K, you get the drift. In short, the fraction of people who manage to complete a course delivered by some of the best scholars in the world is anywhere from 1 in 20 to 1 in 100. After all, self-discipline and the art of learning have to be acquired. Universities allow the students to learn them the hard way by failing, struggling, and catching up. If being an Eklavya was so easy, Eklavya would not have made it into history in the first place!Recent evidence makes this concrete. David Strömberg and his co-authors tracked some 27,000 Chinese schoolchildren aged 12 to 18, roughly 80% of whom had taken to using models like DeepSeek. Within six months their homework scores had risen by 18%, and the time spent on each assignment had fallen from 64 minutes to 45. So far so good. But at exam time, those same pupils scored 20% below classmates who had never used AI. Most telling of all, the old relationship inverted: homework scores used to predict exam performance, and now the pupils with the best homework are the likeliest to stumble in the exam. A randomised experiment in Turkish classrooms points to the remedy—the damage largely disappears when the AI is set up to give teacher-designed hints rather than answers. In short, the irresistible temptation to fetch an answer immediately—much like scrolling reels to kill time—sounds the death knell of learning. Since much of the payoff in the labour market lies precisely in the harder skills, the relevance of the university is likely to persist.There is another challenge with self-learning. Most academics at good universities have far better information about their students than any online platform and can and do design courses that are better suited to their tastes, abilities, and contexts. For example, at ISB, a course on antitrust policies covers a range of cases from the US and India; a course on Indian National Financial Systems goes deep into the Indian economy through the lens of cutting-edge research in economics. I am yet to come across a place outside the university system where one can learn the foundational principles of these topics without wasting hours on obscure and irrelevant material.Second, there is a fundamental question: Does one attend a university only to be taught by professors? Here, I cannot do better than ancient Sanskrit wisdom.आचार्यात्पादमादत्ते पादं शिष्यः स्वमेधया। पादं सब्रह्मचारिभ्यः पादं कालक्रमेण च॥You learn a quarter from the teacher, a quarter through your own intellect, a quarter through fellow classmates, and a quarter from the passage of time. The internet at its best replaces only the teacher’s quarter—and even that I doubt; the other three quarters are what the campus is for. If one switches to a self-learning model, would it be so easy to find fellow classmates who are driven by shared interests, passions, and energy to learn?VS Naipaul once wrote, in, “we make ourselves according to the ideas we have of our possibilities.” A good university reveals to us our possibilities, our challenges and limitations; it exposes us to people better than us and opens our horizons to the opportunities that await us. Skipping university education comes at the cost of denying yourself the opportunity to learn seemingly unrelated and unimportant subjects, the opportunity to engage in intellectually stimulating conversations with your classmates, and above all, the. The unstructured time, the enduring friendships and debates, transform us from adolescents to adults, to people. As Oreopoulos and Salvanes show Schooling creates adults of the kind we need; the robots who’d maximise productivity can be provided by technology.The obsession with finding the “use case” for every course, every lecture, is rather counterproductive. As Steve Jobs, the patron saint of dropping out, said in his famous Stanford commencement speech:And finally, even if one accepts all these benefits, are the costs—time lost and the tuition paid—worth it? Do graduates get paid significantly more? To slightly paraphrase the apocryphal quote of Mark Twain, the reports of the death of the college premium—the additional salaries that college graduates receive relative to their non-college peers—are greatly exaggerated. For example, in a recent article in the Financial Times , John Burn-Murdoch highlighted how the hourly wage premium for university graduates in the US has begun to slip: from a peak of roughly 85% to below 80% today. Unfortunately, such statistics are not available for India, so we must base the arguments mostly on estimates from the West.Focusing on the decline, though, risks losing the bigger picture: a university education still pays a significant premium, and is likely to keep doing so.Still, I must concede one point. The perception that university education has stopped being useful is shaped by recent studies showing rising graduate unemployment in the US and a collapsing graduate job market in the UK . Over the past few decades, as the belief about the “college-premium” got cemented, universities floated several “soft” undergraduate programmes to earn quick money. It is no surprise that people graduating from such degrees would eventually struggle in the labour market. The median early-career salary (ages 22–27) of computer science graduates in the US is $87,000 ( NY Fed data ), while it can be as low as $43,000 for some other disciplines. Indeed, the falling average premium may say less about the democratisation of technical knowledge than about the rapid rise of degrees whose worth the labour market is yet to discover. Several empirical studies establish that even taking the costs into account, most undergraduate education in rigorous fields pays off heavily . The problem is not university education; it is the choice of discipline!Echoing Towles’ protagonist in the opening quote, it may be seductive to embrace a paradigm shift after listening to the confident predictions about the demise of the university model. But it would be rather foolish to play the deck of one’s life, to make choices that will shape your life for decades to come, listening to confident projections about a very uncertain world. It is natural to feel encumbered by the gravity of looming changes in the world that awaits us. We must take comfort in the fact that people have always felt it, in 1960, 1980, 2000, and today. As I was graduating, my PhD advisor David Pearce from New York University gave me a piece of advice that has remained the mantra of my life. One evening in his office, discussing my plans for the years ahead, David said, “Aditya, just take care of the pennies, and the pounds will take care of themselves.” The chances are, if I had not gone to a university, I wouldn’t have learned this, let alone practised it. This was not a part of any curriculum. And that is the beauty of university education: the chance interactions that shape our lives are likely to remain important as long as humans continue to teach humans.
Article Summary: People have started questioning the worth of a university education. They contend that the university model is outdated today due to rapid technological advancements. A good university education teaches us how to learn and not what to learn. Neither AI nor most jobs will teach that.

Article Title: AIIMS removes uterus of 98-cm-tall woman through keyhole surgery
Article Text:
A 44-year-old woman endured extreme menstrual cramps attributed to deep pelvic endometriosis and adenomyosis. (Pic Credit: ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A 44-year-old woman, just 98 cm tall and weighing 22 kg, has undergone laparoscopic hysterectomy at AIIMS , with doctors adapting the surgical approach to minimise fracture risks from severe osteoporosis and address anaesthesia challenges linked to her exceptionally small stature.The woman, who has been living with osteoporosis, or fragile bones, since 2019, had suffered from extremely painful menstrual periods for nearly a year. The pain disrupted her daily life, forcing her to rely frequently on painkillers. Investigations revealed deep pelvic endometriosis and adenomyosis, a condition in which tissue similar to the uterine lining grows outside the uterus or within its muscular wall.Prof Neena Malhotra, head of Obstetrics and gynaecology said that the patient recovered well and was discharged on the third day after surgery.Given her age, bone fragility and high blood pressure, hormonal treatment was not considered feasible.Doctors recommended removing the uterus to relieve her symptoms. Teams from gynaecology, endocrinology and anaesthesia jointly assessed the risks before proceeding with minimally invasive surgery.“Minimally invasive surgery is now routine for most hysterectomies, but operating on an adult woman of this size, with severe bone weakness and hypertension, poses unusual challenges,” said Prof K Aparna Sharma from the department of obstetric and gynaecology.A major concern was positioning the patient. The conventional lithotomy position, in which the legs are raised and supported, could have exposed her lower back and thigh bones to fractures.“Due to short stature along with severely fragile bones, standard lithotomy position for hysterectomy could have put her at risk of lower back and thigh bone fractures. There was a need for utmost care in proper positioning and cushioning during surgery,” said Prof Rajesh Khadgawat of the endocrinology department.At the request of the patient and her family, the team opted to perform the procedure with her lying flat on her back, taking precautions to minimise injury.“The uterus was enlarged due to adenomyosis, and the uterus and ovaries were stuck to the adjacent intestines, while the space in her abdomen was very limited. We were able to complete the hysterectomy successfully through the laparoscopic route in around 90 minutes,” said Prof Reeta Mahey, who performed the surgery.
Article Summary: A 44-year-old woman, just 98 cm tall and weighing 22 kg, has undergone laparoscopic hysterectomy at AIIMS. The woman, who has been living with osteoporosis, or fragile bones, since 2019, had suffered from extremely painful menstrual periods. Investigations revealed deep pelvic endometriosis and adenomyosis.

Article Title: IMD launches WebGIS-based decision support system to improve cyclone disaster preparedness
Article Text:
The India Meteorological Department has launched an advanced WebGIS platform designed to boost disaster preparedness against cyclones.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: As an additional disaster preparedness tool to support ground-level action ahead of cyclones, India meteorological department (IMD) has launched an interactive WebGIS-based platform that will serve as a decision support system (DSS), bringing critical cyclone warnings and marine weather information together in one place.The system will help users, including disaster management authorities, govt agencies and the general public, better understand potential hazards and their likely impacts. It aims to bridge the gap between weather forecasts and their practical application, enabling better preparedness, timely action and enhanced public safety during cyclones and other severe weather events.The launch took place during the bi-annual pre-cyclone exercise meeting for the post-monsoon season (Oct-Dec) under the chairmanship of Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, director general of meteorology, IMD, last week. The DSS platform for the public isavailable on the websites of IMD and regional specialised meteorological centre (RSMC).“Through interactive maps and visualisations of cyclone tracks, intensity, winds, rainfall, storm surge and rainfall forecasts for river catchments, the platform helps users access relevant information and make informed decisions,” said the ministry of earth sciences (MoES) in a statement.IMD has taken a number of steps in recent years to continuously enhance the capabilities in monitoring, numerical modelling and forecasting of the hazards associated with cyclones, and demonstrated its capability to provide early warning for cyclones with high precision. It has, over the years, emerged as the best in the world for the accuracy of cyclone predictions, reporting zero error on the landfall point and timing.A cyclone is an intense vortex or a whirl in the atmosphere with very strong winds circulating around it in an anti-clockwise direction in the Northern Hemisphere and in a clockwise direction in the Southern hemisphere. The word "Cyclone" is derived from the greek word “Cyclos" meaning the coil of a snake. Tropical cyclones are also referred to as 'Hurricanes' over Atlantic Ocean, 'Typhoons' over Pacific Ocean, 'Willy-Willies' over Australian Seas and simply as 'Cyclones' over north Indian ocean.On an average, out of five cyclones developing over the north Indian ocean (NIO) comprising bay of Bengal and Arabian sea annually, about three to four of them make landfall causing loss of life and property. Low - lying coastal belts of West Bengal, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry are more prone to the impact of these systems.The number of deaths due to cyclones has, however, decreased significantly in the recent past, as a result of the improvement in the early warning capabilities of IMD.
Article Summary: The system will help users, including disaster management authorities, govt agencies and the general public, better understand potential hazards and their likely impacts. The launch took place during the bi-annual pre-cyclone exercise meeting for the post-monsoon season.

Article Title: 'Could not prevent regime change within own party': Devendra Fadnavis mocks Uddhav Thackeray
Article Text:
Fadnavis hits back at Uddhav

Also Read |

(with ANI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sunday hit back at Uddhav Thackeray for backing calls for a “regime change” in India, saying the Shiv Sena (UBT) president had failed to prevent a regime change within his own party.“First of all, Uddhav Thackeray could not prevent a regime change within his own Shiv Sena, so I do not know what other regime change he is talking about. The moment his party abandoned Hindutva and the ideology of Hindu Hriday Samrat Balasaheb Thackeray, such turmoil erupted within the party that those who wanted to follow Balasaheb Thackeray’s principles formed the real Shiv Sena,” Fadnavis told reporters in Nagpur.Fadnavis was referring to the June 2022 split in the undivided Shiv Sena, which led to the formation of two factions, one each led by Uddhav Thackeray and Maharashtra deputy chief Minister Eknath Shinde.The chief minister asserted that any regime change in India could take place only through elections, not through street protests.“I have made it very clear: Stop fighting against the Constitution of India. Decisions in this country will be taken in Parliament and in accordance with the Constitution, not on the streets.In a democracy, governments are decided through elections,” he said.Fadnavis expressed confidence that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government would return to power in 2029 and called on the opposition to win public support to secure an electoral victory.“Today, Narendra Modi’s government is in power, and it will be elected again. But if you want a regime change, you must contest elections, win the hearts of the people and secure an electoral victory. Those who dream of bringing about a regime change in India by disregarding the Constitution, as witnessed in Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Pakistan, will never succeed in their intentions,” the chief minister added, referring to the youth- and student-led movements that toppled incumbent governments in three of India’s neighbouring countries in recent years.Fadnavis’ comments came a day after Uddhav Thackeray backed recent calls by activists and opposition leaders for a regime change in India, arguing that denying people the right to express their views through elections and protests would leave them with no option but to seek a change of government.“If you take away our right to express our views through elections and protest, then we're standing up just to overthrow this government,” the Shiv Sena (UBT) chief said.The former chief minister's remarks come amid a political row over references to regime change by opposition leaders and student activists during ongoing protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, student activist and All India Students Association (AISA) president Neha Bora, and Congress spokesperson Pawan Khera have publicly used or discussed the phrase “regime change” at conferences and press briefings in connection with the protests.
Article Summary: Devendra Fadnavis hits back at Uddhav Thackeray for backing calls for a “regime change” in India. Maharashtra chief minister says Thackerays failed to prevent a regime change within his own party. He says any regime change in India could take place only through elections.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan (PTI Photo)

-

Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Article Title: New video captures Tiger Shroff's assassination bid: 3 men fire 7 shots, a gun jams in between
Article Text:
(Image Credit: X) Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility on social media for the attack.

Actor Ignored Warnings

Tiger attack: 15 teams tracing shooters





MUMBAI: In yet another instance of a gangland attack on a film personality, unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants repeatedly fired at a car carrying actor Tiger Shroff and his driver Firdaus in Juhu around 7 pm Sunday, injuring Firdaus on his hand and a fan standing nearby who sustained bullet wounds near his chest.Seven shots were fired in all. The actor who was leaving after attending a birthday party at Pushpa Narsee Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery, escaped with “minor abrasions” from pieces of shattered glass from the vehicle’s windscreen.Two persons identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, and claiming to be affiliated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, took responsibility for the attack in a voice note posted on social media.Amid political reactions questioning the city’s law and order situation, CM Devendra Fadnavis took a briefing from police commissioner Deven Bharti and sought strict action. He also rang Tiger Shroff and assured him saying, “We are all with you.”The incident took place barely 350 metres away from Juhu police station. The vehicle was slowly exiting the venue when two of the assailants, standing amidst a crowd of curious onlookers, sprang in front of the car and opened fire repeatedly.At least one bullet went through the shattered glass of the vehicle. Juhu police said the three assailants, in white shirts, fled in seconds towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station on a bike kept idling by their accomplice.Also read: ‘Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger’: Video shows seat switch as Tiger Shroff takes the wheel after attack Despite being injured, Shroff’s driver emerged from the vehicle and tried to chase them. A senior doctor at Nanavati Hospital, where Shroff and Firdaus were taken, said initial scans showed a foreign body lodged in the latter’s left hand as a result of a bullet injury. He is likely to undergo surgery.In a purported video going viral on social media, one of the two shooters appears unable to fire when he is closest to the car window. The gun seemingly jams as he prepares to fire a sixth shot at point-blank range.Police were registering an FIR and seeking details from actor Tiger Shroff about any recent threat calls or warnings after unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants repeatedly fired at his car on Sunday. Fifteen teams have been formed to trace the assailants. Juhu police and Mumbai crime branch officers were examining CCTV footage to identify them and establish their escape route.Also Read: ‘Should focus on actual criminals’: Dipke jabs police after shots fired at Tiger Shroff “Shroff only has minor abrasions,” said a senior doctor at Nanavati Hospital. The actor was in the hospital’s emergency room till the time of going to the press, awaiting doctor’s advice on his discharge and the treatment plan for his driver.The third person injured in the firing—a passerby identified by police as 35-year-old Umesh Charan—sustained bullet injuries on the right side of his chest, according to Dr Chhaya Shinde, dean of BMC-run Cooper Hospital in Juhu. “He is stable at the moment but will need immediate surgery,” said a doctor.In a press release, BMC said the third patient arrived at the Cooper Hospital casualty at 7.10pm with a “history of a gunshot wound sustained at 6.30pm at Vile Parle West while covering a football match featuring Tiger Shroff. “The patient came with an entry wound at 2cm below left nipple,” the release added.Also Read: ‘Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger’: Video shows actor taking wheel after attack Police initially said Shroff suffered slight abrasions from glass fragments after the car’s windows shattered, but DCP (west zone 2) Mohit Garg said the actor was not injured.Meanwhile, the Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility on social media for the attack. The gang claimed Shroff had been targeted as he ignored their warnings and they also threatened to target anyone who works with superstar Salman Khan.Sources said that Shroff had been being tracked by the shooters for a few days.Posted by Lawrence’s aide, Anil Pandit, the message explicitly stated that Pandit and Harman Sandhu took full responsibility for the action taken against the actor. According to the post, the individuals involved had previously contacted the actor with warnings that were allegedly ignored, leading to the latest targeted event.The statement went on to issue a broad warning to members of the Mumbai film industry, threatening that anyone who fails to listen to them or continues to work with Salman Khan will be targeted next. The message concluded with threats directed at rival gang members and was accompanied by several hashtags referencing the Lawrence Bishnoi group and other affiliated associate networks. Police are verifying the social media post and a voice note.Pandit had earlier claimed responsibility for a shooting outside singer Guru Randhawa’s Delhi gym over an alleged Salman Khan connection.The incident evoked alarm within the film and political circles given the previous fatal attack on politician Baba Siddique in Bandra and the incidence of firing at Salman Khan’s Galaxy Apartment in Bandra Bandstand in 2024.Siddique’s son Zeeshan expressed shock and horror at Sunday’s attack on Tiger Shroff, while NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule echoed his fears over the worsening law and order situation in the state.
Article Summary: Unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants repeatedly fired at a car carrying actor Tiger Shroff and his driver Firdaus in Juhu around 7 pm Sunday. The actor escaped with “minor abrasions” from pieces of shattered glass from the vehicle’s windscreen. Two persons identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, and claiming to be affiliated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, took responsibility for the attack.

Article Title: Indiana father left his entire estate to his fiancee; his daughter challenged the will, lost in court, was ordered to pay $22,208 in legal fees and now faces additional appellate fees
Article Text:
Stacia questioned whether her father had signed the will freely and knowingly. (AI image)

What happened after daughter challenged will?

How did the inheritance dispute turn into a $22,208 bill?

Why did the appeal make matters worse for the daughter?

An Indiana woman who challenged her father's decision to leave his entire estate to his fiancee has lost her case and now faces a growing legal bill. According to the court document, Stacia Davis was ordered to pay $22,208.18 in attorney fees after failing to prove that her father's will was invalid. On Wednesday, the Indiana Court of Appeals upheld that decision and ordered her to pay additional fees for the appeal. The final amount of those extra charges has yet to be determined.At the centre of the dispute was Larry Davis, who died in 2022 at the age of 79. In a will signed nearly two years before his death, Larry had decided that everything he owned would go to his fiancee, Michelle Tressler. The couple had been living together since 2012.The decision meant his three adult children, Sherry, Scott and Stacia, would receive nothing unless Tressler died before him. She was still alive when Larry died, leaving her entitled to inherit his estate under the will.Stacia questioned whether her father had made that decision freely and with a clear understanding of what he was signing. Her challenge began a lengthy court dispute.Following Larry's death in 2022, the court accepted the will and appointed Tressler to manage his estate.Stacia challenged it the following month, claiming her father might not have been mentally capable of making a will and raised allegations of pressure and fraud.The case eventually reached a hearing in February 2025, when the court heard from Stacia, Tressler and two women whose signatures appeared on the will.Both witnesses confirmed that the signatures were genuine. Although neither could remember all the details of the signing, their testimony supported the document's validity.Another document submitted during the hearing raised further questions about Stacia’s case. The affidavit, supposedly signed by one of the witnesses, cast doubt on whether the woman had actually witnessed the signing. However, when questioned in court, the woman said the signature on the affidavit was not hers.Stacia said the document had arrived unexpectedly by post and that she did not know who had sent it. The lower court nevertheless found the affidavit fraudulent and criticised her decision to continue pursuing the case.The court also found that she had not provided acceptable evidence proving her father was mentally incapable of making the will or that Tressler had forced or improperly influenced his decision.The challenge did not only concern who would inherit Larry's property. It also affected the process of managing what he had left behind.In July 2024, the court removed Tressler from responsibility for the estate after finding delays in its administration. Attorney Robert W. York was appointed to take over as special administrator.As the dispute continued, legal expenses increased. The lower court recorded 431 entries across the two connected cases and found that much of the prolonged litigation was linked to Stacia's actions.Judges also criticised requests for documents that had added to the expenses without producing useful evidence for the case.When the lower court rejected Stacia's challenge in 2025, it decided that she should personally bear part of the legal costs rather than leaving the estate to pay everything.York had sought $26,198.61 in attorney fees. After examining the expenses, the court ordered Stacia to pay $22,208.18. The remaining amount was to be paid from the estate.Stacia challenged this order as well, but the appeals court found that the lower court had sufficient grounds to make her pay.Stacia had been represented by a lawyer during the earlier proceedings but handled her appeal herself. Her submissions created another set of problems.The appeals court found that she had included documents that had never been accepted as evidence during the original hearing. Her written arguments also failed to provide several required references to the court records.The judges identified a more serious issue involving the legal cases she cited to support her arguments. Some of those cases did not exist at the references she provided, while others were real but unrelated to the points she was making. Despite these problems, the court chose to consider her arguments.The judges ultimately agreed with the earlier decision that Larry's will was valid. They also upheld the order requiring Stacia to pay $22,208.18.However, the court went further. It found that her appeal involved serious problems with both the arguments and the way the case had been presented, justifying another award of attorney fees. The case has now been returned to the lower court to calculate how much Stacia must pay for the appeal.
Article Summary: Stacia Davis was ordered to pay $22,208.18 in attorney fees after failing to prove that her father's will was invalid. At the centre of the dispute was Larry Davis, who died in 2022 at the age of 79. In a will signed nearly two years before his death, Larry had decided that everything he owned would go to his fiancee.

Article Title: Patrick Mahomes’ mom Randi Mahomes announces major career news as she expands Sports Parent Academy with major Miami event
Article Text:
Patrick Mahomes and Randi Mahomes (Image via Getty Images)

Randi Mahomes announces new Sports Parent Academy event in Miami

Patrick Mahomes’ success highlights his mother’s work behind the scenes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Randi Mahomes is turning her experience as the mother of an NFL superstar into an opportunity to help other families navigate youth sports. While her son, Patrick Mahomes , continues to lead the Kansas City Chiefs through the 2026 season, Randi is preparing a new event that puts young athletes and their parents in the spotlight. Her latest announcement marks another step forward for her Sports Parent Academy, a venture built around the challenges families face while supporting young sporting talent. The upcoming Miami gathering will bring athletes, parents and families together for conversations that reach beyond the playing field.Randi Mahomes has announced the Ultimate Sports Parent Experience, scheduled for October 24 in Miami. The event will be organised alongside Sports Parent Academy and Katalyst Fit, bringing together athletes and sports families for an afternoon of discussions, personal stories and interactive activities.Sharing the news on social media, Randi revealed her excitement about the gathering.“I’m so excited to announce that I’ll be hosting The Ultimate Sports Parent Experience alongside @sportsparentacademy and @katalystfit in Miami on October 24th!”She added, “We’re bringing together athletes, sports parents, and families for an afternoon of meaningful conversations, inspiring stories, and interactive experiences.Whether you’re raising a young athlete or navigating the journey yourself, there’s something here for the whole family.”The event reflects Randi’s growing interest in supporting parents who want to help their children succeed in competitive sports. Her work focuses on the family side of an athlete’s journey, including the pressures, decisions and responsibilities that often remain hidden from public view.Randi founded Sports Parent Academy in 2025. The online platform offers courses and resources designed to help parents understand the demands of raising young athletes. The new Miami event extends that mission into an in-person setting where families can learn from shared experiences.Patrick’s attendance remains uncertain. Article Title: Tiger Woods introduced his children to golf: How Sam and Charlie are shaping the next chapter of his sporting legacy
Article Text:
Tiger Woods returns to golf course after DUI case as new video offers first look at his comeback since March arrest

Details on Tiger Woods’ children Sam and Charlie and how they forge separate paths

Sam Alexis Woods balances school and family legacy

Charlie Axel Woods takes the competitive golf route

Tiger Woods supports his children's individual ambitions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tiger Woods’ impact on golf goes far beyond his record-setting accomplishments, major wins and decades of dominance on the PGA Tour. The 15-time major champion has also passed the game down to his children, Sam Alexis Woods and Charlie Axl Woods, providing them with opportunities to play competitive golf while developing interests of their own.But the next chapter of the Woods family sporting legacy is heading in two different directions. Sam has taken the academic route at Stanford University while Charlie has compiled a competitive junior golf resume and signed with Florida State University. Their paths show that Tiger’s influence still determines the family’s relationship with golf without necessitating that the two children take the same routes.Tiger Woods has two children from his ex-wife, Elin Nordegren. They have a daughter, Sam Alexis Woods (born 2007), and a son, Charlie Axl Woods (born 2009). Both children were introduced to the sport at an early age, with one of golf’s most recognizable faces as their father, but their interests went in different directions.Tiger’s busy professional schedule also colored the family’s experience with golf. Sam has previously said she associated the sport with being away from her father due to his tournament commitments.Instead of jumping right into golf as a competitive endeavor, she sampled other sports, such as soccer and track and field.Charlie became interested in athletics at an early age and found himself drawn more and more to golf. He played with his father in professional exhibition events, giving him the chance to learn by direct experience and to be introduced to the competitive environment.Their many options underscore an important distinction: being Tiger Woods’ kids affords an unusual link to golf history, but it does not dictate how either will shape a future. While Sam has made a name for himself through education and personal interests, Charlie is looking for opportunities to compete at the collegiate level.Sam Alexis Woods has lived a relatively low-key life considering how connected she is to one of the most famous athletes on the planet. Her educational journey has become a major part of her story, with Stanford University being a notable link to her father's university days.Tiger went to Stanford before turning pro in 1996, and was one of the top collegiate players of his generation. She’s at the same university as her dad, so there’s a family connection there, but her focus is academic, so it’s a different sort of experience from the sporting career of her dad, Sam.Golf is not the only sport that has interested Sam. As a child, she played soccer and took up track, broadening her interests outside her father’s professional world. Her story illustrates that a family’s exposure to sport doesn’t necessarily result in a commitment to the same sport.Those moments put her in the public narrative of Tiger’s career without having to become a professional golfer herself. They also demonstrated how family members can assist sporting milestones by supporting and participating rather than competing.Where Sam is now is a compromise between keeping her own goals and staying linked to the legacy of her father. With her Stanford education in her back pocket, she’s heading a different way than Charlie’s competitive golf dreams, but she’s still a part of the sport that influenced much of her childhood via major family events.Since there’s no public info about her longer-term career aspirations, it’s important to distinguish between confirmed educational info and speculation about what she might do after graduating.Charlie Axel Woods took a more direct route to competitive golf, honing his game through junior tournaments, high school championships and playing alongside his father. His tournament results have helped cement his place among young golfers, but his surname has also brought attention to his progress.Charlie made his PNC Championship debut with Tiger in 2020 at age 11. The tournament, which pairs major champions with family members, gave the father and son a chance to compete together on a recurring basis. They were the runners-up in 2021, an example of how they could be a contender in a family competition while sharing the course.The next big step came Feb. 10, 2026, when Charlie announced his verbal commitment to play collegiate golf at Florida State University in 2027. The ruling means he will continue his college career at a different school than Stanford, where Tiger played before turning pro and where Sam is studying.The Florida State golf program has produced some great players, including major winner Brooks Koepka. Charlie’s commitment is therefore an opportunity to develop in a competitive college setting while following his individual objectives in the sport. A verbal promise is not the same as actually going through the official process of enrolling in college.Tiger has also talked about how college recruitment has evolved, saying that communication between players, families and coaches has been much faster than during his own recruitment in the 1990s. He has said that being part of Charlie’s decision-making is an opportunity to see the options that his son has gained through his performances.Tiger's role in the sporting lives of his children goes beyond sharing tournament experiences or teaching them golf. He publicly backs Sam’s soccer exploits and Charlie’s golf drills, a nod to a philosophy that allows both kids to chart their own course.Charlie will always be in the spotlight due to his father's achievements, including 15 major championships and 82 PGA Tour wins. Yet in collegiate golf, his performances, consistency and development will be judged on their own merits. Sam’s academic journey, too, hints at the Woods family legacy reaching beyond professional rivalry.Tiger's success does not decide the fate of either child. Sam can keep on building her professional and academic identity, and Charlie gets a chance to develop his competitive game at Florida State. Their differing choices show how a sporting legacy can be inspirational, without the next generation needing to follow the same career path.So for Tiger Woods, the next chapter isn’t about whether Charlie will play professional golf someday or whether Sam will become more involved in the sport. It’s also about seeing both kids grow into themselves, while still keeping a connection to the game that has defined so much of his life.Charlie prepares for college golf, while Sam heads to Stanford to continue her education; their paths suggest two different ways of continuing the Woods family story. Ultimately, their progress will be defined by their individual choices, their achievements and their interests, not simply their famous surname.
Article Summary: Tiger Woods has two children from his ex-wife, Elin Nordegren. They have a daughter, Sam Alexis Woods, and a son, Charlie Axl Woods. Sam has taken the academic route at Stanford University while Charlie has compiled a competitive junior golf resume and signed with Florida State University.

Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, has remained loyal to the team ever since he was drafted close to two decades ago. Amid the new season, there have been concerns about Stephen Curry’s fitness after his injury plagued season last time. Now, Golden State Warriors’ head coach Steve Kerr has hinted that Stephen Curry might not play all the matches in the new season.A few days ago, while speaking to reporters, the Golden State Warriors’ head coach Steve Kerr said, "We'll start trying to map out, week by week, what's what…But to be really frank, every year we run into this (situation) where, if we have a bunch of games stacked together, back-to-backs, we have fans that buy tickets expecting to see Steph — usually Steph, sometimes other players, people expecting to see vets — and then we have a back-to-back, and we don't play 'em. ”Golden State Warriors’ head coach Steve Kerr added, “So, I would just come out and tell the fans out there to be mindful when you're buying the tickets of the schedule. Take a look. Because we've got not just Steph but multiple vets we are going to try and manage, because it's the only way we can do this."The four time NBA champion Stephen Curry has not responded to the speculations yet as he has sparked concern about a new injury.For the unversed, during an open practice scrimmage on October 18th, Stephen Curry planted his right foot awkwardly and left the floor limping. While it sparked major concern about Stephen Curry aggravating his injury from the last season in his right knee, head coach Steve Kerr quickly reassured fans after speaking with Curry in the training room, stating that "he's fine."Stephen Curry’s Golden State Warriors are all set to open their 2026–27 regular season against the Los Angeles Lakers on Wednesday, October 21. While the injury is minor, team officials will continue to monitor his status over the coming days to determine if he will be cleared for the season opener.In the last season, Stephen Curry was limited to playing just 43 games out of 82 due to a combination of ankle, quadriceps, and knee injuries.The four time NBA champion also sustained "runner's knee" (patellofemoral pain syndrome) and bone bruising in his right knee which sidelined him for two full months between February and April.As the Golden State Warriors navigate through an injury plagued roster, all eyes remain on Stephen Curry.
