Article Title: ‘Writhe in pain’: Video shows injured fan being rushed to hospital after Tiger Shroff firing
Article Text:
The injured fan was identified as 35-year-old Umesh Charan.





MUMBAI: A video of an injured fan being rushed to hospital in an autorickshaw after gunshots rang out at actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai’s Juhu has surfaced on social media.The footage shows bystanders helping the wounded man into the vehicle as he appears to writhe in pain, capturing the aftermath of a shooting that left three people injured.In an apparent gangland attack targeting a film personality, unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants fired seven rounds at a car carrying Shroff and his driver, Firdaus, near Pushpa Narsee Park in Juhu around 7 pm on Sunday.Firdaus sustained a bullet injury to his hand, while a fan standing nearby suffered gunshot wounds to his chest. Shroff escaped with minor abrasions caused by shattered glass, police said.The injured fan was identified as 35-year-old Umesh Charan.According to Dr Chhaya Shinde, dean of BMC-run Cooper Hospital in Juhu, Charan sustained bullet injuries on the right side of his chest. “He is stable at the moment but will need immediate surgery,” a doctor said.In a press release, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) said Charan arrived at Cooper Hospital’s casualty department at 7.10 pm with a history of a gunshot wound sustained around 6.30 pm in Vile Parle West while covering a football match featuring Shroff.The release said he had an entry wound about 2 cm below the left nipple.Police initially said Shroff had suffered minor abrasions from glass fragments after the car’s windows shattered. However, DCP (West Zone 2) Mohit Garg later clarified that the actor had not been injured.Despite being shot, Shroff’s driver emerged from the vehicle and attempted to chase the attackers.A senior doctor at Nanavati Hospital, where Shroff and Firdaus were taken, said initial scans showed a foreign body lodged in Firdaus’s left hand following the bullet injury. He was likely to undergo surgery.The attack unfolded barely 350 metres from Juhu police station.The car was moving slowly as it exited the venue when two assailants, who had been standing amid a crowd of onlookers, suddenly stepped in front of it and opened fire repeatedly. At least one bullet pierced the vehicle’s shattered glass.According to Juhu police, the three assailants, dressed in white shirts, fled within seconds towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station on a motorcycle kept ready by an accomplice.The actor was leaving a birthday party at Pushpa Narsee Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery, when the firing took place.Two people identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, and claiming links to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, later took responsibility for the attack in a voice note posted on social media.
Article Summary: Footage shows bystanders helping the wounded man into the vehicle as he appears to writhe in pain. Unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants fired seven rounds at a car carrying Shroff and his driver, Firdaus, near Pushpa Narsee Park in Juhu. The injured fan was identified as 35-year-old Umesh Charan. He sustained bullet injuries on the right side of his chest.

Article Title: Puppets, war stories and cultural encounters at BRICS Theatre Festival
Article Text:
A still from the Vietnamese play Steel Land, which was showcased on the second day of the BRICS Theatre Festival

PUPPETS THAT HAD THE AUDIENCE CHEERING

The Russian puppet show had the younger audience captivated

WHAT TRAVELS ACROSS LANGUAGES?

A still from the play Samudra Manthan

'THEATRE CONNECTS US BEYOND WORDS'

South African educator Tandi Buchan at the BRICS opening ceremony

-- Anvita Singh





From a Russian puppet show that featured puppets appearing to breathe fire and performing acrobatics to a Vietnamese production exploring the themes of war and peace, BRICS Theatre Festival, inaugurated by the Minister of Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat brought different narratives to the stage from October 12 to 14. Held under the theme of Shared Stories, Shared Futures, the three-day festival featured 11 plays from nine countries -- India, Thailand, Indonesia, Russia, Iran, Vietnam, South Africa, Kazakhstan and Ethiopia -- alongside multiple academic sessions and discussions, encouraging future cultural collaborations.The first day featured the Hindu mythological story of Samudra Manthan and an academic session, while the second half of the day was filled with the energetic Thai Khon masked dance-drama based on the Ramakien (a Thai epic derived from the Ramayana ) and the Indonesian play Iluh Tana (Tears of the Earth), which used the metaphor of a mother to explore the damage caused to the planet from mindless extraction and careless waste disposal.The second day presented a Russian puppet show which was no less than a spectacle that regaled the adults and the children alike, drawing a sea of phone cameras, giggles and whistles. An ape puppet was greeted with particular enthusiasm, while a sequence in which a puppet appeared to breathe fire as the lights dimmed proved a highlight.Later in the night, a Vietnamese production, Land of Steel, offered a solemn experience where the story explored the Indochina War (1946–1954), and the US-Vietnam War (1955-75).A Vietnamese artiste, Ho Van Nhan, described its central message as one of "sacrifice, love and above all peace." "I hope that the audiences can understand our history."For South African artistes, watching Samudra Manthan in Hindi did little to obstruct the understanding of the story."The communication was very clear, even though we didn't understand what was being said," artiste Milu said, praising the performers' use of their bodies to convey emotion. "I think the story was easy to follow, even if the details weren't there for us." "But in terms of what was happening, how we were meant to feel, everything felt very clear," Imitha, another South African artiste, added.Explaining what stayed with her after the performance, Milu mentioned, "When we spoke to the Thailand team, they were telling us about their traditional dancing. Something we've never seen before. I keep going back to the details of the costumes and how it's used in the performance."These exchanges reflected the festival's larger ambition to bring artists and audiences into contact with unfamiliar performance traditions. Speaking about the idea behind the festival's curation, National School of Drama director Chittaranjan Tripathy said, "We wanted to reflect the diversity of theatrical traditions and contemporary concerns across participating countries."For South African delegate and educator Tandi Buchan, the value of such encounters extended beyond the performances themselves."Theater skills teach us how to have agency, to adapt quickly and be flexible." Reflecting on the growing dominance of artificial intelligence, Buchan stated that theatre helps to "bring more feeling from one human to another, connecting us beyond words. So I'm hoping that will be reflected in our production."The festival concluded on October 14 with Louha Purush, an NSD Repertory Company production on the life and legacy of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
Article Summary: The three-day festival featured 11 plays from nine countries -- India, Thailand, Indonesia, Russia, Iran, Vietnam, South Africa, Kazakhstan and Ethiopia. The first day featured the Hindu mythological story of Samudra Manthan and an academic session. The second day presented a Russian puppet show which was no less than a spectacle.

Article Title: Where are Lawrence and Anmol Bishnoi? Tiger Shroff firing puts gang in focus
Article Text:

Where are Lawrence and Anmol Bishnoi?

Tiger Shroff firing : Seven rounds fired near Juhu police station

Bishnoi gang claims responsibility, threatens Salman Khan's associates





MUMBAI: Lawrence Bishnoi is lodged in Gujarat’s Sabarmati Central Jail, while his younger brother Anmol Bishnoi is in Delhi’s Tihar Jail.Their names have returned to the spotlight after two men claiming links to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang took responsibility for the firing at actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai’s Juhu area.Lawrence Bishnoi is lodged in Sabarmati Central Jail in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Despite being behind bars, his alleged criminal network has come under scrutiny over claims that gang operations continue through associates outside prison.His younger brother Anmol is lodged in Tihar Jail in New Delhi after being deported from the United States in November 2025. He is an accused in the murder of former Maharashtra minister and NCP leader Baba Siddique, who was shot dead in Mumbai in October 2024.Anmol was also taken into custody in a case concerning an alleged nexus between criminal gangs in India and the Babbar Khalsa International organisation.The firing took place around 7pm on Sunday, October 18, as Shroff was leaving Pushpa Narsee Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery, after a birthday gathering. The location was barely 350 metres from Juhu police station.Three motorcycle-borne assailants, dressed in white shirts, opened fire at the actor’s car as it was leaving the venue.Seven rounds were fired. The attackers fled towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station, with one accomplice waiting on a motorcycle. A video circulating on social media appeared to show one shooter’s gun jamming as he attempted to fire another round at close range.Shroff escaped without any bullet injuries but sustained minor abrasions from shattered glass. His driver, Firdaus, suffered a bullet injury to his hand, while a bystander, identified as 35-year-old Umesh Charan, was shot in the chest. The injured were taken to hospital for treatment.Police have formed 15 teams to trace the shooters and are examining CCTV footage to identify those involved.After the firing, two men identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu claimed responsibility in a social media post attributed to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang.Pandit claimed Shroff had been warned earlier but had ignored the warning. The message threatened others in the Mumbai film industry who work with Salman Khan.In an audio message shared by the Mumbai Crime Branch, Pandit also demanded that Salman apologise to Lawrence Bishnoi and the Bishnoi community, threatening the actor and his family if he did not comply.The authenticity of the claims and the alleged gang’s role in the firing are being investigated.
Article Summary: Lawrence Bishnoi is lodged in Sabarmati Central Jail in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. His younger brother Anmol is in Tihar Jail in New Delhi after being deported from the United States in November 2025. He is an accused in the murder of former Maharashtra minister and NCP leader Baba Siddique, who was shot dead in Mumbai in October 2024.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Mumbai-Goa highway crash: 30-year-old killed, 2 cousins injured after Honda City hits gate
Article Text:
30-year-old Akshay Kadam lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man driving his Honda City car was killed and his two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured after the driver lost control over the wheels on the Mangaon-Mahad stretch of Mumbai-Goa highway after crossing Mangaon railway station and veering off the road crashed into the iron gate of an industrial unit.The fatal accident occured on Monday around 3 am, when the three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon and were returning to their respective villages in Mahad taluka.The injured complainant stated in the FIR registered at Mangaon police station that the accused car driver and his cousin had consumed liquor before going for dinner.The deceased driver was identified as Akshay Arjun Kadam, a resident of Nandgaon, Mahad taluka. Those injured are Rohit Rajendra Dhadve (24), working as safety officer at Astriel Life Science Pvt Ltd in Mahad MIDC and his cousin Roshan Dilip Dhadve (24). Both residents of Kembhurli, Mahad taluka.Maruti Andhale, senior inspector of Mangaon said, "As the complainant Rohit Dhadve has stated in the FIR that the accused Akshay Kadam drove the car after consuming liquor along with his cousin Roshan, when they had meet near the bus stop, after which they went to Mangaon for dinner, the Motor Vehicle Act section for drunk driving will be invoked.However, as the accused car driver Akshay Kadam responsible for the car crash had died in the accident, a final closure 'Abated summary' report will be submitted before the Mangaon magistrate court. "As per the FIR by the complainant Rohit Dhadve, on Sept 28 around 1 am, when he was at home, his paternal cousin Roshan spoke to him over mobile, when Roshan's maternal cousin Akshay Kadam accompanying him told Rohit that he had come from Mumbai and asked him to meet near the bus stand at Kembhurli.When Rohit met them at the spot, Roshan and Akshay were consuming liquor inside Akshay's Honda City car. Thereafter, Akshay said, "Let's go to Mangaon to have food and the three of them went in the car with Akshay at the wheels."Roshan was sitting beside Akshay and Rohit on the rear seat. They reached Mangaon around 2 am, where they ate parathas at a road side food stall and took parcel of Khima Pav.Thereafter, they drove for 3 kms towards Indapur and took a U-turn to return to their villages in Mahad.After crossing 300 metres from Mangaon railway Station, Akshay lost control over the wheels and yanking off the road on the right side, he crashed into the iron gate of Sundha Steel Traders industrial unit.Rohit sustained injuries below his left eye, left hand and left knee. Akshay got stuck between the driver's seat and the door. Roshan's left leg was injured.Hearing the loud noice of the car crash, the locals gathered, removed the three injured out of the car and summoned 108 ambulance in which they were rushed to Mangaon sub-district hospital, where Akshay was declared brought dead on arrival.
Article Summary: Akshay Arjun Kadam, 30, lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle on the Mumbai-Goa highway. His two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured. The three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon.

Article Title: Bengaluru artistes bring ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ to life at Dombivli Navratri festival
Article Text:
Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.





DOMBIVLI: A theatrical portrayal of Goddess Durga’s battle against demon Mahishasura offered Dombivli residents a glimpse into India’s traditional performing arts during the Sharadiya Navratri festival.Artistes from Bengaluru presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil.The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale of the goddess’s victory to life.The programme was organised as part of the Navratri celebrations hosted by the Dr Shrikant Shinde Foundation and Shri Navdurga Yuva Mandal at the DNC school grounds in Dombivli East.Kalyan MP Dr Shrikant Shinde, who attended the event, stressed the importance of preserving and promoting traditional art forms that reflect India's cultural heritage.“Artistic performances that preserve our culture and traditions are important. They need encouragement and support so that this rich heritage can be passed on to future generations,” Shinde said.The presentation centred on the story of Mahishasura, whose tyranny threatened the world until Goddess Durga took the form of Mahishasuramardini to defeat him.Through a combination of theatrical expression, dance and devotional elements, the Bengaluru artistes depicted the goddess’s strength and the victory of righteousness over evil.Organisers said the festival seeks to go beyond religious rituals by providing a platform for India's diverse cultural and spiritual traditions. Alongside devotional activities, the programme features performances showcasing different forms of traditional art.At a time when modern entertainment platforms are increasingly popular, such performances offer an opportunity to introduce younger audiences to India's mythological stories and traditional artistic expressions.They also help preserve cultural practices that have been passed down through generations.The Navratri festival has included a range of religious and cultural programmes, including the Navkundatmak Sahasrachandi Mahayag, Haripath, bhajan sessions and devotional music.The organisers have sought to combine religious observances with cultural activities to give visitors a wider experience of the festival.The ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’ presentation added a distinctive dimension to this year's celebrations, highlighting the role of traditional theatre in keeping India's mythological narratives and performing arts alive.
Article Summary: Bengaluru artistes presented ‘Sri Devi Mahishasuramardini’, blending dance, drama, expressive acting and devotion to narrate the triumph of good over evil. The performance drew an enthusiastic response from the audience, with traditional costumes and dramatic sequences bringing the mythological tale to life.

A man and his nephew died after a large mound of mud collapsed on them during well excavation at Rasalwadi near Deulgaon Rasal in Baramati taluka around 11am on Sunday.The accident occurred when the work of placing explosives in the well was underway.The deceased have been identified as Machhindra Ramchandra Rasal (55) and Amol Dhanaji Rasal (27). Article Title: Citizens face weeks of delay for Pune RTO driving tests as slots vanish in minutes
Article Text:
The Alandi Road test track of the Pune RTO

Pune





: Getting a driving test appointment at the city RTO has become a frustrating exercise, with daily slots filling up within minutes and applicants left waiting weeks for a chance to secure their licences.Bavdhan resident Saurabh Singh, whose driving lessons ended on Oct 3, has been trying to book a test through his driving school ever since, without success. “Representatives of the school have been trying every day, but slots are unavailable. I have a brand-new car at home that I want to drive, but the delay is frustrating. I am also worried that I may forget some of the skills I learnt during training,” the working professional said.A senior office-bearer of Jadhav Motor Training School, which operates several branches across Pune, said the situation has left driving schools struggling to secure appointments for their students. “Earlier, slots opened at 6 am, but now they open at 8 am and are filled within 15 to 20 minutes. Applicants seeking licences for both two-wheelers and four-wheelers face particular difficulties. Slots are also released daily instead of being made available for an entire month, as was the practice earlier,” she said.The available appointments are for mid-Nov or early Dec, she added, leaving applicants, including those who need driving licences before moving abroad, in a fix.Vimannagar resident Shobhit Surana, who completed his driving lessons in the last week of Sept, said even approaching RTO officials has yielded no clarity. “I visited the office, but was only told that slots were limited. I am leaving for a five-month work assignment in Dubai after Diwali and am worried about getting my licence in time. Instead of spending quality time with my family during the festive season, I am caught up in this uncertainty,” he said.The Pune RTO currently has 728 daily appointments for driving tests across two-wheelers, four-wheelers, and autorickshaws. Two-wheeler and autorickshaw tests are conducted at the RTO office on Alandi Road, while four-wheeler tests take place at the Institute of Driving Training and Research (IDTR) in Bhosari.Kondhwa resident Asleen Azad Sheikh, who is struggling to book his final test for an autorickshaw licence, suspected that unauthorised agents were cornering the available slots. “Why should applicants wait more than a month just to take a driving test? Even after passing, getting the licence can take another 10 days. The authorities need to address this urgently,” he said.Pune deputy RTO Swapnil Bhosle acknowledged the shortage, attributing it to recent transport department directives limiting each inspector to 60 tests a day and requiring tests to be conducted under CCTV surveillance. These measures, he said, have reduced daily appointments from the earlier 800–900 capacity. He added that there is no cap on the number of applicants taking learner licence tests, contributing to the pressure in a city that ranks among Maharashtra’s highest in vehicle registrations.To ease the backlog, the RTO has approached Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation ( MSRTC ) to use its automated driving test track in Bhosari, which remains largely vacant outside the corporation’s driver-training requirements. “Talks are in the final stages. We hope to lease the facility, similar to the IDTR arrangement, and start using it this month. This will add 300 to 400 appointments daily and help clear the backlog,” Bhosle said.
Article Summary: The Pune RTO currently has 728 daily appointments for driving tests across two- wheeler, four-wheelers, and autorickshaws. The RTO has approached Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation to use its automated driving test track in Bhosari.

:

Article Title: Elephant dies of anthrax near Coimbatore; carcass incinerated following strict safety protocols
Article Text: COIMBATORE: A female elephant died of anthrax in the Gopanari Reserve Forest under the Periyanaickenpalayam range in Coimbatore district. According to officials, a forest patrol team spotted the carcass at around 4pm on Tuesday. Preliminary observations suggested that the animal had died a day before.Upon inspecting photographs of the carcass, forest officials grew suspicious of a potential anthrax infection. To verify this, a blood smear was collected on Wednesday by forest veterinarians and sent to the district animal husbandry department, which subsequently confirmed that the elephant had died of an anthrax infection.Following orders from the field director and chief conservator of forests (Anamalai Tiger Reserve) along with the district forest officer (in-charge), a 50-metre perimeter around the carcass was isolated, and immediate measures were taken to keep scavengers and other animals away.Upon receiving laboratory confirmation that the elephant had tested positive for the anthrax infection, disposal procedures were initiated on Thursday. Adhering strictly to guidelines laid down by the ministry of environment, forest and climate change (MoEF) and the Tamil Nadu environment, climate change and forests department, the carcass was incinerated in the same place where it was found dead.
Article Summary: A female elephant died of anthrax in the Gopanari Reserve Forest under the Periyanaickenpalayam range in Coimbatore district. A 50-metre perimeter around the carcass was isolated, and immediate measures were taken to keep scavengers and other animals away.

Article Title: Kovai Heroes: This woman has helped scores of birds get a second chance in sky
Article Text:
A resident of Sivananda Colony with a doctorate in environmental science, Vinny turned a childhood passion for birdwatching into a lifelong defence of avian life. (Photo by J Jackson)

Kovai Heroes is a city-wide recognition initiative by The Times of India, presented by Infinium developers to identify, celebrate and honour individuals who are making a positive impact in Coimbatore through their work, service, innovation, leadership or acts of kindness. Education Partner: SSVM Institutions. Associate Partner: Lakshmi Ceramics.





COIMBATORE: Inside a quiet recovery enclosure, a rescued Alexandrine parakeet stretches its wings, testing the flight muscles that have withered after years of captivity. A few cages away, an injured peafowl rests under veterinary observation, recovering from electrical burns sustained on high voltage wires. At the centre of this relentless healing mission is Vinny R Peter, 42, a wetland ecologist whose life’s work revolves around giving birds a second chance in the sky.A resident of Sivananda Colony with a doctorate in environmental science, Vinny turned a childhood passion for birdwatching into a lifelong defence of avian life. As director of community education for the NGO Animal Rescuers, she operates on the frontlines of urban wildlife conservation, bridging community distress calls with rapid medical intervention in partnership with the Tamil Nadu forest department.For Vinny, urban skies present a labyrinth of hazards caused by human activities -- lethal manja threads, concrete sprawl and exposed electrical transformers.Vinny says some of the deepest wounds she has seen stem from illegal confinement. “Parakeets are born to fly, not to mimic human names,” she says.“Birds possess the fundamental right to flight. Alexandrine parakeets naturally fly up to 40 kilometres a day.We clip their wings and tail feathers, and keep them confined in tiny iron cages for years,” she says.Her team frequently rehabilitates parakeets confiscated from roadside fortune-tellers -- often with severely damaged beaks -- as well as domestic pets trapped in human habits. One rescued bird could only mimic the roar of a motorcycle exhaust; another called out the name “Meenu” repeatedly. Through sustained public awareness drives, several residents have voluntarily surrendered caged birds after realizing that possessing protected wild species violates wildlife laws.Operating out of the Avian Recuperation Centre in the District Forest Officer complex on the Mettupalayam Road, Vinny and her volunteer network coordinate care with the forest department’s frontline staffers and specialized veterinarians. Equipped with in-house diagnostic tools like X-ray units, the facility handles complex fractures, open trauma, dehydration in migratory birds and orphaned chicks. Over the past 15 years, the organization has rescued and sheltered more than 13,000 native and migratory birds, even providing critical care to rare visitors like the endangered Egyptian vulture.However, treatment is only the halfway mark. Every bird is rehabilitated in specialized flight enclosures designed to rebuild flight stamina before being released back into native canopies.Beyond immediate medical rescue, Vinny actively focuses on shaping future mindsets. Through school tours at the recuperation centre and urban outreach campaigns, she educates young students on urban biodiversity, bird-friendly landscaping and the simple act of setting out water bowls during summer. By teaching the next generation to view wild birds not as pets to possess but as vital architects of the ecosystem, Vinny ensures that Coimbatore’s skies remain alive with full-throated songs of happy birds.
Article Summary: Vinny R Peter is a wetland ecologist whose life’s work revolves around giving birds a second chance in the sky. As director of community education for the NGO Animal Rescuers, she operates on the frontlines of urban wildlife conservation. Over the past 15 years, she has rescued and sheltered more than 13,000 native and migratory birds.

Article Title: Elephant trapped in slush at Gunderipallam dam near Erode; rescue operations under way
Article Text:
Photo by S Parthiban





ERODE: A female elephant got trapped in slush at the Gunderipallam dam near Gobichettipalayam in Erode district, prompting a major rescue operation by forest and fire service personnel on Sunday.Wild animals have been frequently entering the dam vicinity in search of drinking water due to acute water scarcity in the forest. The water level in the Gunderipallam dam, located in the T N Palayam forest range, has dropped in recent weeks. In the early hours of Sunday, a female elephant that came to the dam to drink water got stuck in the slush in the exposed portion of the reservoir. “Unable to free itself, the animal struggled for several hours and was trumpeting in distress,” said a forest officer from the T N Palayam forest range.On being alerted by residents, officials and staff from the T N Palayam forest range and personnel from fire and rescue services rushed to the spot and launched rescue efforts.As the elephant had become exhausted after being trapped in the slush for several hours, teams began efforts to pull it out using ropes and an earthmover. However, the rescue operation suffered a setback when an earthmover deployed for the task got stuck in the muddy terrain.The incident delayed rescue operations.Forest authorities made alternative arrangements by bringing in another earthmover to rescue the elephant. A veterinary team from Sathyamangalam has been mobilised to provide medical assistance and monitor the elephant’s condition.
Article Summary: Wild animals have been frequently entering the dam vicinity in search of drinking water due to acute water scarcity in the forest. The water level in the Gunderipallam dam, located in the T N Palayam forest range, has dropped in recent weeks.

Article Title: Little handlers, big paws
Article Text:
Demonstration of Belgian Malinois Best known as a police or security dog steal the show

Madurai:





The dogs were the contestants, but young handlers and a Belgian Malinois demonstrating security skills stole the spotlight at the Madurai Canine Club’s 41st and 42nd All Breed Championship Dog Show at Viraganur on Sunday.The event featured around 350 dogs representing 50 breeds, including several rarely seen in Madurai. A competition for young handlers aged 12 to 16 was a key attraction, with children demonstrating their ability to control and present dogs of different sizes before judges. Eight youngsters received prizes based on their handling skills and their dogs’ behaviour.Among the participants was M Chandra, 14, who said growing up with dogs had encouraged him to take part. “I also want to encourage other children my age to adopt and care for dogs,” he said.A Belgian Malinois, a breed commonly used for police and military duties, drew attention with a demonstration by a trainer from a private K9 centre. The session showcased how dogs could be trained for security assignments, including guarding warehouses and detecting suspicious materials.Judges from India and Taiwan evaluated the entries. A Rampur Hound exhibited by Sivaganam from Coimbatore won first prize in Group 11, reserved for native breeds.Rajapalayam, Chippiparai, Kanni, Kombai and Caravan Hounds were among the Indian breeds represented, with special awards for the best Indian breed and puppy.S Ramanathan, secretary of the Kennel Club of India-affiliated Madurai Canine Club, said the event aimed to encourage responsible pet ownership and raise awareness about caring for stray dogs. Visitors also got to see Rottweilers, Boxers, Afghan Hounds and Great Danes.
Article Summary: The Madurai Canine Club’s 41st and 42nd All Breed Championship Dog Show at Viraganur on Sunday featured around 350 dogs representing 50 breeds. A Belgian Malinois, a breed commonly used for police and military duties, drew attention with a demonstration by a trainer from a private K9 centre.

Article Title: Dhanush welcome to AIADMK: Rajendra Balaji
Article Text:
Rajendra Balaji





Virudhunagar: AIADMK leader and former minister K T Rajendra Balaji on Saturday said actor Dhanush would be welcomed into the party with both hands, amid speculation over the actor's political future.Speaking to reporters after an AIADMK event in Sivakasi , Balaji however refrained from confirming whether the actor intended to join the party. Article Title: Land brokers arrested for murder of elderly woman in Salem
Article Text: SALEM: The Salem city police arrested two land brokers on Tuesday in connection with the murder of an elderly woman and the theft of her gold jewellery.N Janabai, 74, of Muniyappan Samy Koil Street in Kitchipalayam, was found strangled to death at her residence on Monday night. The murder came to light when her son, Sathish Kumar alias Senthil Kumar, 50, returned home after work. He found that her gold jewellery, weighing seven sovereigns, was missing.The Kitchipalayam police registered a case.Salem city police commissioner Joshi Nirmal Kumar formed a special team to investigate the case. Inquiries revealed that land broker A Sampath Kumar, 55, of Masinaickenpatti and S Vairamani, 70, of Kitchipalayam in the city murdered the woman and stole her seven sovereigns of gold jewellery. Later, the duo pledged the jewellery at a pawn shop. “The stolen ornaments have since been recovered,” said a police officer.Police found that Janabai had sold a portion of her land a few months ago and had been frequently approached by land brokers regarding the sale of her remaining properties. Sampath Kumar and Vairamani were among those who had allegedly visited her in connection with land transactions.Further investigations are under way.
Article Summary: N Janabai, 74, of Muniyappan Samy Koil Street in Kitchipalayam, was found strangled to death at her residence on Monday night. Her son, Sathish Kumar alias Senthil Kumar, 50, found that her gold jewellery, weighing seven sovereigns, was missing. The stolen ornaments have since been recovered.
